claims.reason: runtime-supervisor.cjs:1796-1805 awaits tunnelProxyEnvironmentProvider before reserving tunnelControlQueue; overlapping providers can make a later invocation install and run first.

stopChild waits for exit or close and then unconditionally calls terminateOwnedProcessTree(child, SIGKILL); Unix process-tree termination uses the stale negative PID without a post-settlement identity check.

cancelRecoveries aborts only startup/recovery controllers; ordinary tunnel-control children remain in tunnelControlChildren until close, while forceStopOwnedRuntime neither cancels that set nor settles it before queueing another stop.

roots.title: Tunnel control queue reservation occurs after environment await
roots.trigger: Two runTunnelCommand calls overlap while tunnelProxyEnvironmentProvider is pending; the later provider resolves first.
roots.fix: Reserve the queue successor synchronously before the first await, then resolve proxy environment only after the invocation owns its predecessor slot; retain cancelled slots until predecessor release.

roots.title: stopChild can kill a reused Unix process group after child settlement
roots.trigger: The owned child settles, its PID/process-group number is reused, and stopChild reaches its unconditional final SIGKILL.
roots.fix: Remove the final kill after settlement or require a live, identity-bound ownership check before signaling; keep forced termination before settlement bounded and reported.

roots.title: Forced shutdown does not own cancellation of ordinary tunnel control children
roots.trigger: An ordinary stop or cleanup control child remains active when shutdown falls into forceStopOwnedRuntime; its queue slot is held until close while force cleanup starts another stop.
roots.fix: Track a supervisor cancellation handle for every control child, terminate all tracked children in the force path, wait for close settlement, and report unresolved children as partial cleanup.
